metadata.methods_description: EEG data were collected during six tasks: three passive tasks (resting state with eyes open/closed fixation, surround suppression with flashing peripheral disks, and movie watching) and three active tasks requiring participant responses (contrast change detection with feedback, sequence learning with age-appropriate designs, and computerized symbol search). Behavioral responses including reaction times and accuracy were recorded during task performance. Data quality control ensured absence of corruption, presence of necessary task events, and readiness for preprocessing. Events were annotated using Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED version 8.3.0) to enable systematic meta-analysis.

citation_details.title: REVE: A Foundation Model for EEG - Adapting to Any Setup with Large-Scale Pretraining on 25,000 Subjects
citation_details.author: Yassine El Ouahidi, Jonathan Lys, Philipp Thölke, Nicolas Farrugia, B. Pasdeloup, Vincent Gripon, Karim Jerbi, Giulia Lioi
citation_details.abstract: Foundation models have transformed AI by reducing reliance on task-specific data through large-scale pretraining. While successful in language and vision, their adoption in EEG has lagged due to the heterogeneity of public datasets, which are collected under varying protocols, devices, and electrode configurations. Existing EEG foundation models struggle to generalize across these variations, often restricting pretraining to a single setup, resulting in suboptimal performance, in particular under linear probing. We present REVE (Representation for EEG with Versatile Embeddings), a pretrained model explicitly designed to generalize across diverse EEG signals. REVE introduces a novel 4D positional encoding scheme that enables it to process signals of arbitrary length and electrode arrangement. citation_details.title: EEG Foundation Challenge: From Cross-Task to Cross-Subject EEG Decoding
citation_details.author: Bruno Aristimunha, Dung Truong, Pierre Guetschel, Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Isabelle Guyon, Alexandre R. Franco, M. Milham, Aviv Dotan, S. citation_details.abstract: Current electroencephalogram (EEG) decoding models are typically trained on small numbers of subjects performing a single task. Here, we introduce a large-scale, code-submission-based competition comprising two challenges. First, the Transfer Challenge asks participants to build and test a model that can zero-shot decode new tasks and new subjects from their EEG data. Second, the Psychopathology factor prediction Challenge asks participants to infer subject measures of mental health from EEG data. For this, we use an unprecedented, multi-terabyte dataset of high-density EEG signals (128 channels) recorded from over 3,000 child to young adult subjects engaged in multiple active and passive tasks. We provide several tunable neural network baselines for each of these two challenges, including a simple network and demographic-based regression models. citation_details.abstract: Deep learning and large public datasets have recently catalyzed the proliferation of AI models for processing brain recordings. citation_details.title: CoMET: A Contrastive-Masked Brain Foundation Model for Universal EEG Representation
citation_details.author: Ang Li, Zikai Wang, Liuyin Yang, Zhenyu Wang, Tianheng Xu, Honglin Hu, M. V. Hulle
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive technique for recording brain activity, widely used in brain-computer interfaces, clinic, and healthcare. Traditional EEG deep models typically focus on specific dataset and task, limiting model size and generalization. Recently, self-supervised brain foundation models have emerged and been applied to various downstream tasks. Nevertheless, these models still have limitations: current SOTA models typically rely on masked reconstruction strategy; however, EEG features of adjacent channels are highly correlated, which causes the pre-training to overly focus on low-dimensional signal-similarity features in local regions and neglect the global discriminative patterns vital for downstream tasks. citation_details.title: OmniEEG-Bench: A Standardized Evaluation Benchmark for EEG Foundation Models
citation_details.author: Zilin Lu, Zongsheng Li, Xinke Shen, Kexin Lou, Ying Xin, Xiaoqing Chen, Shinan Wang, Xiangyu Chen, Jiahao Fan, Chenyu Huang, Xin Xu, Zhoujie Hou, Chen Wei, Quanying Liu
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) supports a variety of brain-computer interface (BCI) tasks ranging from brain-state monitoring to human-LLM interactions. EEG foundation models are emerging, but evaluation remains fragmented due to heterogeneous datasets and nconsistent task protocols. Here, we introduce OmniEEG-Bench, a unified benchmark and downstream task roadmap for EEG foundation models (FMs). It organizes evaluation of EEG FMs into six task families spanning (i) signal reliability, (ii) biometrics and disease, (iii) consciousness and state, (iv) cognition and emotion, (v) naturalistic stimulus decoding, and (vi) motor and interaction, introducing a new generation of tasks not systematically benchmarked in prior EEG FM work. citation_details.title: Zero-Shot Neural Priors for Generalizable Cross-Subject and Cross-Task EEG Decoding
citation_details.author: Baimam Boukar Jean Jacques, Brandone Fonya, Nchofon Tagha Ghogomu, Pauline Nyaboe, Kipngeno Koech
citation_details.abstract: The development of generalizable electroencephalography (EEG) decoding models is essential for robust brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and objective neural biomarkers in mental health. Conventional approaches have been hindered by poor cross-subject and cross-task generalization, owing to high inter-subject variability and non-stationary neural signals. We address this challenge with a zero-shot cross-subject decoding framework on the large-scale Healthy Brain Network dataset, benchmarking a convolutional neural network baseline, a hybrid LSTM, and a Transformer-based foundation model. To adapt the Transformer for regression while averting catastrophic forgetting, we propose a novel progressive unfreezing strategy. The baseline yielded an nRMSE of 0.9991, whereas our fine-tuned Transformer achieved 0.9799 on unseen subjects. This work advances scalable, calibration-free EEG decoding for computational psychiatry and behavioral prediction.

citation_details.title: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 4
citation_details.author: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig
citation_details.abstract: The Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG Release 2 dataset comprises high-resolution electroencephalogram recordings from 152 children and adolescents (ages 5-21 years) performing six distinct cognitive and perceptual tasks, including resting state, passive viewing tasks (surround suppression, movie watching), and active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). The dataset includes behavioral responses, hierarchical event descriptors (HED) for systematic meta-analysis, psychopathology measures (P-Factor, Attention, Internalization, Externalization) derived from the Child Behavior Checklist, and personalized electrode locations, providing a rich resource for investigating neural correlates of typical and atypical development. This Release 2 represents a subset of the larger Healthy Brain Network project.

citation_details.title: Brain Semantic Communication: Brain Semantics Computation and Robustness Evaluation
citation_details.author: Zi Wang, Ang Li, Guiying Xu, Tianheng Xu, Honglin Hu
citation_details.abstract: In this paper a Brain Semantic Communication (BSC) framework is proposed for the Internet-of-Brains, where raw EEG is replaced by task-agnostic semantic representations extracted via a self-supervised foundation model. Trained with masked autoencoding on diverse EEG data, the model enables direct cognitive inference—without signal reconstruction—across heterogeneous downstream tasks. To assess practical viability, we evaluate semantic robustness under uncoded additive white Gaussian noise across SNRs. Results on motor imagery, imagined speech and visual decoding reveal a key insight: semantic resilience is task-dependent, with sensory-driven tasks (e.g., SSVEP) remaining stable even at −20 dB, while high-level cognitive tasks degrade sharply below 0 dB. This underscores the need for cognition-aware joint source-channel coding in future BSC systems. Our work establishes a foundation for efficient and noise-resilient brain-to-machine communication.

citation_details.title: CoCoT-EEG: Contrastive-Pretrained Multiscale Convolutional Transformer for EEG Decoding
citation_details.author: Gabriel Mahuas, Victoria Shevchenko, Ugo Tanielian, Yassir Bendou, Richard Gao
citation_details.abstract: Self-supervised pretrained foundation models (FM) have shown early promise for non-invasive electroencephalogram (EEG) decoding applications. Many recent large-scale models converged on the approach of tokenizing raw EEG followed by masked reconstruction pretraining. However, this recipe has been shown to be suboptimal for data, like EEG, with high noise amplitude and information confined to limited dimensions such as narrow frequency bands. Building on this insight, we develop a novel contrastive-pretrained EEG model with multiscale temporal convolution input layers and Transformer encoder blocks (CoCoT). CoCoT matches or beats state-of-the-art reconstruction-pretrained EEG models on extensive benchmark decoding tasks with heterogeneous electrode configurations. Furthermore, CoCoT trained from scratch outperforms previous single-task decoding models and even rivals pretrained models, showcasing the architecture's flexibility and data efficiency. citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a noninvasive approach for examining neurophysiological correlates of dimensional psychopathology, yet systematic evidence across EEG paradigms and feature granularities remains limited. Here, we develop a granularity-aware EEG feature pipeline that organizes multi-scale descriptors into global, regional, and channel levels. Using the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) cohort, we evaluate the prediction of four psychopathology dimensions: p-factor, internalizing, externalizing, and attention problems, across four EEG paradigms. Given the heterogeneity of pediatric psychopathology and the moderate reliability of questionnaire-derived scores, this setting represents a challenging feasibility test rather than a clinical screening scenario. citation_details.author: A. Yuce, Chris Leffler, Sarun Varghese, M. Spiliopoulou, Sebastian Stober
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models aim to learn generalizable representations from large-scale brain recordings. However, the role of temporal feature extractors and whether pretrained time-series foundation models (TSFMs) can be effectively transferred to this setting remains underexplored. We conduct a controlled comparison of three temporal feature extraction strategies, including a linear baseline, a convolutional encoder, and a frozen pretrained TSFM (MOMENT), within a unified EEG foundation model. We evaluate their impact on representation quality using two downstream tasks: motor imagery and emotion recognition. Results reveal different trends across the evaluated benchmarks. citation_details.title: PRiSE-EEG: A Prior-Guided Foundation Model with Depth-Stratified Experts for Cross-Paradigm EEG Representation Learning
citation_details.author: Wei Xiong, Jiangtong Li, Kun Zhu, Jie Li
citation_details.abstract: EEG foundation models aim to learn reusable representations across heterogeneous paradigms, yet existing approaches often use uniform adaptation mechanisms and are typically reported under separate downstream fine-tuning protocols. citation_details.title: Q-DIVER: Integrated Quantum Transfer Learning and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search with EEG Data
citation_details.author: J. Park, Yeong-Duk Park, Jiook Cha
citation_details.venue: 2026 International Conference on Quantum Communications, Networking, and Computing (QCNC)
citation_details.abstract: Integrating quantum circuits into deep learning pipelines remains challenging due to heuristic design limitations. We propose Q-DIVER, a hybrid framework combining a largescale pretrained EEG encoder (DIVER-1) with a differentiable quantum classifier. Unlike fixed-ansatz approaches, we employ Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search to autonomously discover task-optimal circuit topologies during end-to-end finetuning. On the PhysioNet Motor Imagery dataset, our quantum classifier achieves predictive performance comparable to classical multi-layer perceptrons (Test F1: 63.49 %) while using approximately 50 × fewer task-specific head parameters (2.10 M vs. 105.02M). These results validate quantum transfer learning as a parameter-efficient strategy for high-dimensional biological signal processing.

citation_details.author: Asif M S, S. K., A. P. Vinod
citation_details.venue: 2025 Asia Pacific Signal and Information Processing Association Annual Summit and Conference (APSIPA ASC)
citation_details.abstract: Attention is one of the most crucial cognitive factors for a high-quality living and survival for a person. Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based attention estimation has been explored by researchers as a promising approach for non-invasive monitoring of a person's mental focus and vigilance. In this paper, we present a novel approach for EEG-based attention quantification using an image contrast feature, generalized Contrast-to-Noise Ratio (gCNR) adopted from the domain of biomedical ultrasound. The work validates the effectiveness of gCNR in attention quantification, using the EEG data collected from 14 healthy subjects using the proposed experimental paradigm. The performance of the gCNR feature is further tested on Healthy-Brain Network (HBN)-R1, a larger open-source dataset of 136 subjects. citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography(EEG) signals are important indicators of brain activity and states of mind. This study conducts an in-depth exploration of the Healthy Brain Network EEG Dataset, presenting key findings and insights derived from the analysis. The significant features extracted are mean, standard deviation, variance, power spectral densities (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma), entropy, wavelet energy, and the Hurst exponent. Early results indicate that Beta and Gamma power components of greater frequency have high correlations with cognitive processing, whereas lower frequency bands like Delta and Theta are associated with relaxation and sleep. Entropy and wavelet energy also play a part in discriminating between active and passive brain states. citation_details.title: Neuroelectromagnetic Data Archive and Repository: Open-source platform analysis
citation_details.author: Tracy Brandmeyer, Anna Riggs, Viraaj Reddi, Hayley Sullivan, Choonhan Youn, Subhashini Sivagnanam, Kenneth Yoshimoto, Russell A. Poldrack, Nell Hardcastle, Christopher Markiewicz, A. Majumdar, Yahya Shirazi, Dung Truong, Scott Makeig, A. Delorme
citation_details.abstract: Open data infrastructures are rapidly reshaping the landscape of neuroscience by enabling greater reproducibility through transparency, reusability, and collaboration, thus providing a foundation for sustainable and scalable scientific progress. This paper presents a systematic audit of the Neuroelectromagnetic Data Archive and Repository (NEMAR), a platform supporting the sharing and reuse of EEG, MEG, and iEEG datasets standardized through the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) format. Drawing on a detailed analysis of over 300 publicly available datasets, we assess the composition, metadata quality, and population coverage of data in NEMAR. Our findings reveal significant momentum in data sharing practices, particularly in EEG, and highlight key challenges, including inconsistent metadata, underrepresentation of clinical populations, and variable adherence to data standards. These insights highlight the importance of targeted support for policy and cultural development to ensure open repositories like NEMAR are not only accessible but also equitable, reusable, and scientifically robust.

citation_details.abstract: Reproducibility package for: The Geometry of Conscious States: Direction and Dispersion in EEG State Transitions Companion code for:Howie, S. J. (2026e). The Geometry of Conscious States: Direction and Dispersion in EEG State Transitions. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19600377 OVERVIEW This deposit is the single source of truth for every numeric result in the geometry paper. Each headline number traces to a specific script in analyses/ and a specific output file in outputs/canonical/. Running scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze from a clean checkout reproduces every figure, table, and cited value from the deposited per-subject feature JSONs in outputs/. The paper treats conscious-state transitions as directions and dispersions in a five-dimensional state space whose axes are the framework's Phi components: I_A (interaction density), organization (1 minus normalized graph entropy), memory (I_M), recursive feedback I_R, and relative alpha power. I_R is the canonical normalized spectral radius of the thresholded Granger-causality graph. The central findings are the near-orthogonality of the sleep and propofol exit directions, the wider per-subject angular dispersion of the propofol pathway, and the equal-weights composite choice. DATASETS (about 314 subjects after QC; per-subject feature JSONs bundled) Sleep (ANPHY-Sleep, OSF thsqg), n = 28 — sleep exit (Wake to N3)Cambridge propofol (Chennu et al.), n = 19 — propofol exit (Baseline to Moderate)DS005620 (OpenNeuro ds005620), n = 20 — light-sedation hybrid exitSRM (OpenNeuro ds003775), n = 111 — normative healthy-adult baselineHBN (OpenNeuro ds005505), n = 136 — relative-alpha swap verification SELF-CONTAINED REPRODUCTION bash scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze reproduces every cited value from the bundled per-subject feature JSONs in outputs/ (no external testsuite needed). Then: python scripts/verify_outputs.py re-derives every value in outputs/canonical/paper5_numbers.csv against its committed reference within tolerance and exits nonzero on any mismatch. The raw-EEG preprocessing in pipelines/ is optional and needed only to regenerate the feature JSONs from the source datasets listed in datasets/manifest.md. CONTENTS (selected) analyses/trajectory_geometry.py — group-mean 5D vectors, magnitudes, inter-paradigm angles.analyses/trajectory_stats.py — per-subject trajectory statistics and inferential outputs (bootstrap CIs, label-permutation p-values, dispersion-variance tests).analyses/angular_dispersion.py — per-subject trajectory dispersion.analyses/swap_effect_sizes.py — relative-alpha swap per-channel effect sizes.analyses/weighted_geomean_analysis.py — Fisher-LDA weights versus equal weights (characterization; equal weights are what the framework uses).pipelines/ — optional raw-EEG reprocessing per cohort._framework_core/ — shared constants, signal IO, and Phi-component computation.scripts/run_all.sh, scripts/verify_outputs.py — pipeline driver and numeric verification gate.outputs/ — bundled per-subject feature JSONs and canonical result tables. REQUIREMENTS Python 3.11 with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, and MNE (see environment.yml or requirements.txt). MNE is needed only for raw-EEG reprocessing; the analyze stage runs from the bundled feature JSONs. CROSS-DEPOSIT NOTE This deposit's _framework_core is the pre-retirement five-channel vintage (persistence I_M present), matching the geometry the paper analyzes. The Paper 4 deposit ships a same-named core that retired I_M to a four-channel Phi, so the two stamp different pipeline hashes and their raw Phi and C x 100 are not cross-deposit comparable. This deposit is internally self-consistent with its own core. VERSION v4 (2026): documentation hygiene only; no numeric or code-behavior change. Removed two dead references from the README layout and added the Phi-vintage cross-deposit caveat. Version 3 (May 2026) bundled _framework_core at the top of the zip, renamed the cohort feature JSONs to the series convention, and added the verify_outputs.py numeric gate. citation_details.title: 5D Conscious State Test Suite: Reproducibility Package for The Geometry of Conscious States
citation_details.author: Spencer Howie
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Standalone reproducibility package for the manuscript "The Geometry of Conscious States: A Five-Dimensional Framework" (Howie, 2026, Zenodo, forthcoming). The code and committed feature data regenerate every numeric result cited in that manuscript — group-mean state vectors and magnitudes, inter-paradigm angles, per-subject trajectory dispersion statistics, the pooled-baseline Φ_ref calibration (n=67), and the equal-weighted versus Fisher-weighted geometric-mean comparison — from five publicly available EEG datasets: ANPHY Sleep (OpenNeuro ds003768, n=28) — endogenous acute exit Cambridge propofol (n=19) — pharmacological acute exit ds005620 light propofol sedation (n=28) — partial pharmacological exit ds003775 SRM normative (n=111) — pooled-baseline anchor ds005505 HBN (n=136) — eyes-open / eyes-closed developmental contrast used in the channel-substitution audit Running bash scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze from the committed feature JSONs reproduces every canonical output; python scripts/verify_outputs.py numerically checks each of the twenty pinned values against the frozen reference in outputs/canonical/paper5_numbers.csv. Raw BIDS preprocessing (CAR re-reference, epoching, feature extraction) is also included under pipelines/ and is invocable if users want to replicate from raw data. The composite implemented is the equal-weighted geometric mean of five channels — interaction asymmetry, organizational specificity (1 − H_norm), inverse memory depth (1 − I_M), recursive integration, and relative alpha power — with the Consciousness Index reported as 100·Φ₅/(Φ₅ + Φ_ref). Canonical Φ_ref = 0.716. The implementation lives in analyses/_common.py. Full directory layout, dataset provenance, and per-number output mapping are documented in the deposit's README.md and MANIFEST.md.

Running scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze from a clean checkout reproduces every figure, table, and cited value from the deposited per-subject feature JSONs in outputs/. The paper treats conscious-state transitions as directions and dispersions in a five-dimensional state space whose axes are the framework's Phi components: I_A (interaction density), organization (1 minus normalized graph entropy), memory (I_M), recursive feedback I_R, and relative alpha power. I_R is the canonical normalized spectral radius of the thresholded Granger-causality graph. The central findings are the near-orthogonality of the sleep and propofol exit directions, the wider per-subject angular dispersion of the propofol pathway, and the equal-weights composite choice. DATASETS (about 314 subjects after QC; per-subject feature JSONs bundled) Sleep (ANPHY-Sleep, OSF thsqg), n = 28 — sleep exit (Wake to N3)Cambridge propofol (Chennu et al.), n = 19 — propofol exit (Baseline to Moderate)DS005620 (OpenNeuro ds005620), n = 20 — light-sedation hybrid exitSRM (OpenNeuro ds003775), n = 111 — normative healthy-adult baselineHBN (OpenNeuro ds005505), n = 136 — relative-alpha swap verification SELF-CONTAINED REPRODUCTION bash scripts/run_all.sh --stage analyze reproduces every cited value from the bundled per-subject feature JSONs in outputs/ (no external testsuite needed). Then: python scripts/verify_outputs.py re-derives every value in outputs/canonical/paper5_numbers.csv against its committed reference within tolerance and exits nonzero on any mismatch. The raw-EEG preprocessing in pipelines/ is optional and needed only to regenerate the feature JSONs from the source datasets listed in datasets/manifest.md. CONTENTS (selected) analyses/trajectory_geometry.py — group-mean 5D vectors, magnitudes, inter-paradigm angles.analyses/trajectory_stats.py — per-subject trajectory statistics and inferential outputs (bootstrap CIs, label-permutation p-values, dispersion-variance tests).analyses/angular_dispersion.py — per-subject trajectory dispersion.analyses/swap_effect_sizes.py — relative-alpha swap per-channel effect sizes.analyses/weighted_geomean_analysis.py — Fisher-LDA weights versus equal weights (characterization; equal weights are what the framework uses).pipelines/ — optional raw-EEG reprocessing per cohort._framework_core/ — shared constants, signal IO, and Phi-component computation.scripts/run_all.sh, scripts/verify_outputs.py — pipeline driver and numeric verification gate.outputs/ — bundled per-subject feature JSONs and canonical result tables. REQUIREMENTS Python 3.11 with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, and MNE (see environment.yml or requirements.txt). MNE is needed only for raw-EEG reprocessing; the analyze stage runs from the bundled feature JSONs. CROSS-DEPOSIT NOTE This deposit's _framework_core is the pre-retirement five-channel vintage (persistence I_M present), matching the geometry the paper analyzes. The Paper 4 deposit ships a same-named core that retired I_M to a four-channel Phi, so the two stamp different pipeline hashes and their raw Phi and C x 100 are not cross-deposit comparable. This deposit is internally self-consistent with its own core. VERSION v4 (2026): documentation hygiene only; no numeric or code-behavior change. Removed two dead references from the README layout and added the Phi-vintage cross-deposit caveat. Version 3 (May 2026) bundled _framework_core at the top of the zip, renamed the cohort feature JSONs to the series convention, and added the verify_outputs.py numeric gate. citation_details.title: EEG Benchmarking Needs a Task Specification Layer: NeuroDoc for Rulebook-Guided, Executable Benchmark Construction
citation_details.author: Chengxuan Qin, Zhige Chen, Shu Peng, Rui Yang, Jiping Cui, Yikai Dong, Jun Li, Liu Peng, ZH Shang, Mingze Tang, Kay Chen Tan, Jianmin Wu
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models increasingly rely on multi-dataset training and evaluation, yet public EEG datasets still lack a shared task specification layer that can turn heterogeneous recordings into reusable benchmark units. Existing standards organize files, metadata, and provenance, but they do not specify EEG tasks under a common language and rulebook, leaving critical task semantics scattered across papers, code, and manual interpretation. We investigate whether heterogeneous public EEG datasets can be standardized through a structured task specification language paired with a shared rulebook. Our methodology represents each benchmark entry as a task document synchronized with an executable task kernel, with the rulebook defining task fields, evidence requirements, document-kernel alignment, review states, and machine-checkable constraints. Using this methodology, we release a community-reviewed EEG benchmark corpus centered on 53 completed and reviewed entries with 245 task definitions spanning diverse paradigms, and we introduce NeuroDoc and NeuroAudit as the operational support layer for rulebook-guided drafting, upgrading, review, amendment, and release management. We further examine whether the resulting benchmark units can be instantiated in a shared downstream setting across four EEG foundation model backbones, providing execution-based evidence for reusable, auditable, and executable EEG benchmarking infrastructure.
